scope: Local investigation only; product source restored after controlled experiment

confirmed.finding: A previous awaited cache write delays later received live snapshots
evidence: Expected responsive assertion fails on main after the second SSE batch is reduced upstream
Current behavior diagnostic holds the update for a controlled 306-309 ms and displays it 5-8 ms after release
Detaching only the cache await allows the same update to display while that write is still held

confirmed.finding: One cache writer blocks warm reads of unrelated conversations
confirmed.evidence: Real HistoryCache with another key already present in memory cannot finish that read until the held write releases the shared mutex

confirmed.finding: Every memory hit and save reserializes retained payloads to recompute cache sizes
confirmed.evidence: At 1250 events and 714319 encoded bytes per entry, warm read p50 is 0.88-1.06 ms with one entry versus 8.22-12.55 ms with twelve across two measured runs

interpretation: CACHE_SAVE and CACHE_READ timers include mutex waiting, not only disk time
The first snapshot is published before its save; the delay applies to a subsequent snapshot or initial cache read
The shared lock and full-cache accounting remain in current main after #316, #320 and #325
candidateDesign: Remove cache persistence from the critical path of live snapshot publication
Coalesce pending snapshots per cache key with a bounded writer and preserve generation invalidation, reading positions, monotonic cursors and final flush
Retain per-entry size accounting so a cache hit does not walk every retained conversation
unproven: No claim that all observed phone latency comes from this mechanism
No measured production speedup; detached launch is only a causality experiment, not a final safe fix
reproduce: Historical standalone probe retired in Wave 1
